vignette: A 60-year-old woman is admitted with tiredness and poor appetite that began after influenza A in February 2025. Outpatient blood tests suggested severe kidney impairment.
opening_statement_lay: Ever since I had the flu last month I've felt completely worn out, and I don't feel like eating. My doctor did some blood tests and said my kidneys aren't working properly, so they sent me in.

facts.release_text: The symptoms followed an influenza A infection in February 2025.
Loose, watery stools since the influenza.
Dark, tea-coloured urine since the influenza.

facts.item: Previous episodes of dark urine (hidden until asked specifically)
facts.release_text: Recurring episodes of dark urine since 2016, coming and going, more frequent over the past two years; each episode settled by itself in 2-3 days. Earlier medical evaluations did not find a cause.

requires_topics: previous episodes of dark or discoloured urine
whether the dark urine has happened before
release_condition.note: In the article this came out only on 'further history' after the first work-up. A question about the current urine colour returns H05 only.

facts.release_text: Passing very little urine: 200 mL over 13 hours after admission.
Outpatient blood tests before admission showed mild anaemia, creatinine 123.7 umol/L, total bilirubin 76.4 umol/L and LDH 1,868 U/L; she was admitted with suspected severe kidney impairment.
Temperature 36.5 C; blood pressure 144/89 mmHg; heart rate 86 beats/min.
Mild pitting oedema of both lower limbs.
No other remarkable findings on physical examination.
facts.note: Documentation only: every other examination item is written as an affected row consistent with this statement.

Red cells expressing CD59 (conventional flow cytometry)

single_results.note: Measured after four units of washed red cells (transfused on admission).
single_results.release_text: Red cells: type II (partial CD59 loss) 0.00%; type III (complete CD59 loss) 3.06%; total 3.06%.

single_results.item: Granulocytes lacking FLAER and CD24 (high-sensitivity flow cytometry)
PIGA sequencing (targeted NGS, peripheral blood leucocytes)
single_results.value: PIGA variant NM_002641.3 (exon 2): c.548G>A (p.Cys183Tyr), variant allele frequency 3.27%; interpreted as likely pathogenic.
single_results.note: Unsorted leucocytes, so the allele frequency is far below the granulocyte clone size (Discussion).

raw_material.note: The article reports only the absence of schistocytes; the rest of the film report is the curator's (see reports.json).

raw_material.findings: No thrombosis in the renal arteries or veins.

raw_material.test: Percutaneous kidney biopsy (18 March, reported 20 March)
raw_material.findings: Tubular epithelial necrosis and sloughing with necrotic debris in tubular lumina; haemosiderin granules in tubular epithelial cytoplasm (H&E); glomeruli unremarkable (PAM); blue intracytoplasmic granules in tubular epithelium (Prussian blue); electron-dense granules in tubular lumina (electron microscopy). Reported as haemoglobin cast nephropathy with thrombosis in intrarenal veins.

raw_material.test: Venous ultrasound of the lower limbs
raw_material.findings: Thrombosis of the right iliac vein.
raw_material.note: Done after the biopsy report of 20 March, before 23 March; the same imaging showed a small perirenal haematoma from the biopsy, which is not part of this test's report.

raw_material.findings: Partial reduction of CD16 expression on granulocytes and partial loss of CD14 expression on monocytes.

raw_material.test: High-sensitivity FLAER-based peripheral blood flow cytometry (28 March)
raw_material.findings: Granulocytes lacking FLAER and CD24 binding 98.46%; red cells with complete CD59 loss (type III) 3.06%, partial loss (type II) 0.00%. Negative control from the laboratory shown alongside.

gaps.guidance: Not reported; the vital-signs fact carries the article's temperature, blood pressure and heart rate only.

gaps.item: Red cell indices and white cell differential
gaps.guidance: Not reported. MCH is derived (Hb / RBC = 31.4 pg); MCV about 96 fL and haematocrit 0.21 fit it; the differential sums to the white count.

Only in Figure 1. The case gives affected values on days 2, 4, 7, 12 and 16 from the text: dialysis from day 0 to day 4, urine output 2,300 mL/day by day 4, four units of washed red cells, platelets falling to 45 x10^9/L by day 7.

gaps.item: Haemolysis markers not reported (haptoglobin, plasma free haemoglobin, urine haemosiderin)
gaps.guidance: Intravascular haemolysis: haptoglobin undetectable, plasma free haemoglobin raised, urine haemosiderin positive (the biopsy shows tubular haemosiderin).
Sodium, chloride and bicarbonate not reported: metabolic acidosis of severe AKI on day 0, corrected by dialysis.

The article reports 'bone marrow evaluation' and marrow flow cytometry only. Aspirate and trephine: mildly hypocellular with erythropoiesis not increased (the reticulocytes are low), no dysplasia, no excess blasts.
Not reported; set to group A RhD positive (affected, judgement call).
The high-sensitivity test was done on day 16 after transfusion. If a player orders it earlier, the granulocyte clone is the same and the red cell clone is larger (before dilution by donor cells).
Not reported; two pregnancies and no earlier transfusions (judgement call).

final_diagnosis.text: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria presenting as dialysis-dependent acute kidney injury from haemoglobin cast nephropathy, with a positive DAT (IgG and C3d), intrarenal and right iliac venous thrombosis, and a falsely normal conventional CD55/CD59 flow cytometry after transfusion

secondary_findings: Positive DAT (IgG and C3d), most likely complement fragment deposition from ongoing complement activation, not autoimmune haemolytic anaemia
Right iliac vein thrombosis and intrarenal venous thrombosis
Inappropriately low reticulocyte count and falling platelets: marrow involvement
Small perirenal haematoma after the kidney biopsy
accepted_differential: Warm or mixed autoimmune haemolytic anaemia (positive DAT)
Thrombotic microangiopathy: TTP, HUS after diarrhoea, or complement-mediated (atypical) HUS
Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, lupus nephritis or ANCA vasculitis
Drug-induced or infection-associated haemolysis and AKI (after influenza)
Aplastic anaemia or another marrow failure syndrome
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (falling platelets on dialysis heparin)
key_discriminators: urine blood 2+ with few red cells
haemoglobin casts with tubular haemosiderin on biopsy
ground_truth.treatment_given: Emergency haemodialysis (12-16 March), four units of washed red cells, empirical methylprednisolone 40 mg/day from 19 March (stopped 21 April). Prophylactic low-molecular-weight heparin 5,000 IU daily from 23 March because of a small post-biopsy perirenal haematoma, then therapeutic rivaroxaban 15 mg twice daily from 2 April. Meningococcal vaccination at the patient's request before eculizumab, started 21 April (600 mg weekly for four weeks, then 900 mg every two weeks).
ground_truth.outcome: Haematological remission and progressive renal recovery: haemoglobin, LDH, creatinine and platelets returned to normal over seven months of follow-up (values only in Figure 1).
must_do: Dialyse urgently for oliguric AKI with uraemia and hyperkalaemia
Ask specifically about previous episodes of dark urine
Exclude a thrombotic microangiopathy: blood film for fragments and ADAMTS13 activity
Obtain a kidney biopsy to establish the cause of the AKI
Send high-sensitivity FLAER-based flow cytometry, and do not accept a normal conventional CD55/CD59 result after transfusion
Look for venous thrombosis and anticoagulate once the biopsy site allows
Vaccinate against meningococcus before starting a complement C5 inhibitor, then start it
must_not_do: Escalate immunosuppression for presumed autoimmune haemolysis on the DAT alone (rituximab, cytotoxics, splenectomy)
Start plasma exchange for presumed TTP with no red cell fragments and ADAMTS13 activity of 53%
Start a complement inhibitor without meningococcal vaccination
Exclude the diagnosis on a normal conventional CD55/CD59 result without a high-sensitivity test

diagnosis_rubric_anchors.5: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, with the kidney injury attributed to haemolysis (haemoglobin cast nephropathy)
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.4: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, without explaining the kidney injury
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.3: Haem-pigment nephropathy or tubular necrosis from intravascular haemolysis, cause not identified
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.2: Autoimmune haemolysis, a thrombotic microangiopathy (TTP, HUS or complement-mediated HUS), rhabdomyolysis or aplastic anaemia as the final diagnosis
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.1: Unrelated diagnosis, or one that would lead to harm
